clips.title: Dead Code Shouldn’t Exist! How We Removed 28k Lines of Code, One Knip at a Time -Dominik Dorfmeister
clips.why: Dominik Dorfmeister, who maintains TanStack Query, explains how knip decides what is unused: from entry files, along the import graph.
look: Entry files are where knip starts. Anything it never reaches from them is reported.
Think about which ways of using code are not imports at all.
clips.after: Those ways, such as dynamic imports built from strings, are exactly what our verifiers check before the one writer deletes anything.

clips.title: Calling All Mutants: Getting Started with Mutation Testing
clips.why: A short, clear explanation of why coverage does not prove tests catch bugs, and how planting small bugs, mutants, does.
look: Code can be fully covered by tests that would never notice it breaking.
A mutant that survives, because no test fails, shows a real gap.
clips.after: The test-gap routine keeps a new test only if it kills its planted mutant and passes on clean code.

practice.q: Put one night of the dead-code routine in order.
items: knip lists unused files and exports
One read-only verifier per candidate searches for hidden usage
Unsure candidates are dropped; proven ones are kept
One writer deletes at most 10 proven items
verify, check-types and build pass, and the PR shows the proof for each item
practice.why: Find, prove, then one small write: the order keeps every deletion backed by evidence.

practice.q: The dead-code writer changes import { a, b, unused } from "./x" into import { a, b } from "./x". Does the add_code rule reject it?

options.why: The new line only loses a name from the old one. Shortening an import is still a deletion.

options.text: No, a line that only loses names is still a deletion
options.why: The rule rejects new code, not a shorter version of an existing line.
Removing an unused name from an import is exactly the kind of change the routine makes.

practice.q: Finish the dead-code routine's charter rule that rejects any diff adding code.
practice.hint: Two words joined by an underscore.
practice.why: A deletions-only routine that adds code is doing something other than removing dead code, so the false-heal check rejects it.

practice.q: jscpd finds two 80-token date formatters in features owned by different teams, which change for different reasons. What does the duplicates sweep do?

options.text: Merges them, because the code is the same
options.why: Code that looks the same but changes for different reasons is not a real duplicate. Merging ties two things together that should move alone.

options.text: Keeps them apart, because the judges find no shared reason to change
options.why: Only real duplication with the same reason to change becomes a merge proposal.
Both are used. The sweep proposes merges, never deletions.
